title: Cabinet Refinishing in Trenton, FL | Precision Paint
description: Cabinet refinishing in Trenton FL: degreasing, sanding, bonding primer, and sprayed waterborne urethane enamel for a hard, smooth kitchen finish.
heroIntro: A new look for Trenton kitchens and baths without tearing out the boxes, using a urethane enamel that dries hard enough for daily use.

sections.h2: Why cabinet paint fails, and how we stop it
body: Cabinet coatings almost always fail in the same spots: around the range, above the sink, and on the edges your hands grab dozens of times a day. Cooking oil soaks into the old finish there, and paint laid over that residue lets go. Good cabinet refinishing in Trenton FL begins with a dedicated degreaser and a rinse, followed by sanding everything to a uniform dull so the bonding primer has something to hold.
Oak cabinets bring one more step. Their open grain shows through paint as stripes, so we fill the grain when you want a smooth, modern look.

bullets: Doors and drawer fronts removed, labelled, and finished separately
Cabinet boxes degreased, scuffed, and finished in place
Sprayed waterborne urethane enamel for a hard, cleanable film
Hardware reinstalled and doors adjusted at the end

sections.h2: Timing and living with the work
body: Your kitchen stays usable for much of the job, since the boxes are masked and the doors are worked separately. Drying and curing are built into the schedule on your estimate, and we will tell you when the surfaces are ready for normal use. Most projects start one to three weeks after approval.
Colors can be matched from a chip or an existing door, and you see a large sample before we spray.

If your cabinet boxes are solid and the layout works, refinishing usually makes far more sense than tearing out and replacing. You keep the countertops, plumbing, and backsplash in place, and the kitchen is never fully out of service. Replacement makes more sense when boxes are water-damaged, swollen near the sink, or the layout no longer works. During the walkthrough the crew lead checks for swelling and loose joints and tells you honestly which route fits. Hinges and pulls can be reused or swapped for new hardware at reinstallation.

faqs.q: Can you paint oak cabinets so the grain does not show?
faqs.a: Yes. We can grain-fill oak before priming so the finished doors read smooth. Our article on painting oak cabinets explains the trade-offs.

faqs.q: What finish do you use on cabinets?
faqs.a: A sprayed waterborne urethane enamel from premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines, over a bonding primer. The exact product is named on your estimate.

faqs.q: Do you refinish bathroom vanities too?
faqs.a: Yes. Vanities get the same degrease, sand, prime, and enamel process as kitchen cabinets.

faqs.q: Can you change dark wood cabinets to white?
faqs.a: Yes. Big changes from dark wood to light colors get a bonding primer and, when needed, a third coat so the finish covers evenly.
